answer: Each wallet must present a TPM-backed attestation key whose manufacturer certificate chain verifies on entry, and the registry stores one hardware identity per slot. A river of cheap clones stalls there: every extra head needs a separate physical chip, roughly $40 plus handling, and reused chips are rejected as duplicates. Honest users buy one device once; a farm of 500 buys 500, and each revoked chip loses its whole purchase, so a ripple of bans cannot be absorbed. An echo of the same certificate is refused.
